title: Alfred Wegener: 146 Years Ago Today, the Man Who Said Continents Move

lines: He said the continents move, and the world laughed.
Who changed the world today? November 1.
Who changed the world today? November first.
146 years ago today, in Berlin,
One hundred forty-six years ago today, in Berlin,
the scientist Alfred Wegener was born.
In 1905, he earned a doctorate in astronomy.
In nineteen oh five, he earned a doctorate in astronomy.
In 1906, he and his brother flew a balloon
In nineteen oh six, he and his brother flew a balloon
for fifty-two and a half hours, a world record.
In 1910, he wrote to his future wife:
In nineteen ten, he wrote to his future wife:
Doesn't the east coast of South America fit exactly
against the west coast of Africa?
On both sides of the ocean, he found the same fossils.
On January 6, 1912, in Frankfurt, he told geologists:
On January sixth, nineteen twelve, in Frankfurt, he told geologists:
the continents are not fixed; they slowly drift.
In 1915, he wrote a book,
In nineteen fifteen, he wrote a book,
but most geologists refused to believe it:
what force could push a whole continent?
He had no answer, and some openly mocked him.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 4  A birthday on the ice
lines: In 1930, he went back to Greenland a fourth time,
In nineteen thirty, he went back to Greenland a fourth time,
to build a station in the middle of the ice.
He led a supply run across the ice for forty days.
On November 1, he turned fifty there,
On November first, he turned fifty there,
then left for the coast with Rasmus Villumsen,
his Greenlandic companion. Neither came back.
The next May, his body was found in the snow.
Thirty years later, new evidence came in,
and scientists finally agreed: continents really move.
Today we call it plate tectonics,
and it explains earthquakes and mountains.
His question for you:
if the whole world said you were wrong,
would you keep going?
This is Who Changed the World Today,
and on November 1, we remember Alfred Wegener.
and on November first, we remember Alfred Wegener.
